question: Why is backpropagation considered the mathematical engine inside neural network training frameworks?
direct_answer: Because it provides the gradient information needed to update every trainable parameter in a model.
expanded_answer: Modern frameworks can build a computation graph during the forward pass and then use backpropagation to compute parameter gradients automatically. Those gradients are what optimizers like SGD and Adam use to train the network.
common_wrong_ideas: Frameworks train by guessing better weights directly
Backprop is only a theoretical idea, not used in practice
